question: During a lab meeting on gas exchange in the alveoli, which assertion is right?
options: Alveoli pump air actively using muscle contractions.
Gas exchange occurs mainly in the trachea and bronchi.
Alveoli absorb oxygen into the digestive system.
Oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse across the thin alveolar walls.
gold_answer: Oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse across the thin alveolar walls.
notes: Team-authored original item on gas exchange in the alveoli. Passages are team-authored derivations recorded under sciclaim-appx-A. Requires independent annotation and adjudication before any gate result is reported.

positions.answer: Alveoli absorb oxygen into the digestive system.

claims.text: Carbon dioxide diffuses from the blood into alveolar air.

evidence.text: Blood arriving at the lungs carries more carbon dioxide than alveolar air, so it diffuses outward to be exhaled.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes outward carbon dioxide movement, which entails the claim.

claims.text: The diaphragm performs gas exchange inside the alveoli.

evidence.text: The diaphragm ventilates the lungs by changing thoracic volume; diffusion itself occurs passively across alveolar walls.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage assigns the diaphragm a ventilation role, not exchange, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Lung capacity is the same in every adult.

evidence.text: Vital capacity was recorded once per volunteer in the survey.

claims.verdict_rationale: Recording values cannot show all adults are identical, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Alveoli pump air actively using muscle contractions.

claims.text: Alveolar walls are thin enough for rapid diffusion.

evidence.text: The air-blood barrier is about one cell thick on each side, keeping the diffusion distance extremely short.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes an extremely short diffusion distance, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Alveoli convert carbon dioxide into oxygen.

evidence.text: Alveoli only exchange the gases by diffusion; no conversion of carbon dioxide into oxygen takes place there.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage denies any conversion, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Air pollution never reaches the alveoli.

evidence.text: Particle deposition was modeled for the upper airways in the study.

claims.verdict_rationale: Modeling upper airways says nothing about alveolar reach, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse across the thin alveolar walls.

claims.text: Oxygen diffuses from alveolar air into the blood.

evidence.text: Because alveolar oxygen pressure exceeds that in incoming blood, oxygen moves down its gradient into capillaries.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes downhill oxygen movement into blood, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Thicker alveolar walls would speed up gas exchange.

evidence.text: Diffusion slows as wall thickness grows, which is why fluid-filled or scarred lungs exchange gases poorly.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states thickness slows diffusion, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Breathing exercises cure all lung diseases.

evidence.text: Lung function was measured before and after a breathing program in one patient group.

claims.verdict_rationale: One patient group cannot support cures for all diseases, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.
